newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former Alcatel chief fined, given suspended sentence.
newsitem.headline: Former Alcatel chief fined, given suspended sentence.

text.p: The former chairman of French industrial giant Alcatel Alsthom was fined $345,000 and given a three-year suspended jail sentence Tuesday for plundering company funds to pay for security work on his private homes.

Pierre Suard, forced to resign in June 1995 after being placed under judicial investigation, was convicted by a district court in the Paris suburb of Evry of abusing corporate funds and fined two million francs ($345,000).
The court rejected a prosecution call to send him to prison for six months.

Suard, 62, reported to have been France's highest paid chief executive, was also ordered to repay 4.9 million francs ($845,000) to Alcatel Alsthom for the cost of the extensive security systems installed in his three homes.
The former head of the electronics and telecommunications equipment manufacturer, France's second-biggest industrial group, had no comment on leaving court. His lawyer said he would appeal.
Suard had told the court he took the security measures on the advice of the government after the head of carmaker Renault was assassinated by hard-left urban guerrillas in 1986.
